newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordanian stocks fall to ten-week low.
newsitem.headline: Jordanian stocks fall to ten-week low.

text.p: Shares on Jordan's stock exchange fell to a ten-week low on Monday as delay to crucial legislation and anxiety over an attack by a Jordanian on Israelis last week rattled investor confidence, brokers said.
The official Amman Financial Market (AFM) index fell for the eighth consecutive trading day, easing 0.73 points to 152.13, its lowest level since January 5.
Turnover of 770,000 dinars ($1.08 million) was dominated by trade in the blue-chip Arab Bank, which fell 3.75 dinars to 251 dinars after shares worth 482,000 dinars changed hands.
Shares in the bank rose as high as 269 dinars two weeks ago on hopes of a bonus share offer after parliament passed a new companies law cancelling a 15 percent tax on capital increases.

But brokers say the law will not come into force until another bill governing the stock exchange is passed. That bill now faces a long wait to be ratified as parliament will be dissolved on Wednesday ahead of November elections.
"This delay has really affected the psyche on the market," said Nasser al-Amad, head of the United Financial Investments.
He said the killing of seven Israeli schoolgirls by a Jordanian soldier on Thursday had also shaken confidence on the bourse, often a barometer of sentiment in the Middle East peace process.
Jordan Cement Factory and Housing Bank both rose slightly, but overall falling shares outnumbered gainers by 15 to nine. Another 12 shares traded but closed unchanged.
The private Pearl Index of the 45 most-traded shares on the exchange shed 0.33 percent to 79.99 points, 4.08 percent down from the start of the year.
